set_aside.why: The hydrology bundle's signed SWOT lake dataset concept records that the Version D family changes from reprocessing (PGD0, through 2025-04-27) to forward processing (PID0) on 2025-04-28, and its signed river concept records the same two processing identifiers. Everything from that date on is one processing baseline, the request says none of it has been looked at, and it keeps growing, so it is what a later test would want. 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-27 is neither explored nor set aside.

data.question: How well does SWOT river height follow the Baton Rouge gauge, and where does it not?

data.takes: Rules in: pair each pass with a gauge reading inside a stated tolerance, score the changes, name the collection, use the shipped executor. Rules out: scoring the level difference or calling it a bias, a pass matched outside the tolerance, fewer than ten pairs. Warns: the intervals are sampling intervals capped at the count, and the gauge is provisional throughout 2024. It already gives the 2024 change scores at this pair, so those are known, not something to rediscover.

Rules in: reach elevation against a gauge is a confrontation between independent records (discharge would not be). Warns: reach_q is a categorical gate, not a size of error; wse_u is total uncertainty. Says the Version D family carries two processing identifiers, reprocessed and forward.
Used for one fact: the release note places reprocessing through 2025-04-27 and forward processing from 2025-04-28. That is where the set-aside window starts.
Warns: the two product versions differ by metres at this very reach and share no timestamps. Rules out mixing versions in one series. The fixture names Version D and keeps Version C apart.

NOT SIGNED, a draft about lakes. Warns: a satellite-minus-gauge level is mostly the datum; compare changes. Agrees with the signed recipe, so I lean on the recipe and treat this as a second, unsigned voice.
Rules in: say the aggregation level. Everything here is at reach level, one reach against one point gauge 0.44 km away.
About lakes. Takes only that Version C carried a geoid error Version D fixed, one more reason not to join versions.
Where the series comes from and which fields it carries. Nothing is fetched in this exploration: the fixture is already on disk.

data.about: SWOT RiverSP reach_q at this reach (knowledge: datasets/swot-river-lake.md)
data.text: Seen while exploring calendar 2024 at reach 74210000331 against USGS-07374000, Version D, 50 pairs within 15 minutes. The three passes with reach_q 2 all fall at low stage (gauge 1.47 to 3.51 m of a 1.47 to 10.33 m range); their departures from the median level difference have a spread of 0.798 m against 0.162 m for the 47 passes with reach_q 1, and one (2024-10-30, the lowest stage of the year) is 1.776 m low. The product's stated uncertainty for that pass is 0.095 m, the median, so wse_u does not warn of it. The dataset concept says reach_q is a categorical gate and does not say what happens to a comparison when it is not applied. Unflagged passes at low stage are fine (lowest third of stage, 15 pairs, spread 0.078 m), so it is the flag and not low water that marks them.

data.about: SWOT RiverSP dark_frac and wse_u on an unflagged pass (knowledge: datasets/swot-river-lake.md)
data.text: Seen while exploring the same record. One pass with reach_q 1 (2024-03-26, gauge 7.68 m) is 0.939 m above the rest. It has the highest dark_frac of the year (0.692; the next highest third starts at 0.026) and the largest stated uncertainty (wse_u 0.296 m against a median of 0.096 m). So here the quality flag missed a bad pass that dark_frac and wse_u both mark. One pass in one year: enough to warn, not enough to set a threshold. With it and the three flagged passes left out the residual spread about the gain line is 0.082 m, below the product's median stated uncertainty.

data.about: knowledge: recipes/swot-gauge-confrontation.md, the worked example for Baton Rouge 2024
data.text: Seen while exploring. The recipe's worked example scores all 50 pairs: change correlation +0.9567 and change RMSD 0.3823 m, which it reads as about four times the product's stated precision. Recomputed here identically (LOOK-013). With the three passes flagged reach_q 2 left out, the same scores are +0.9896 and 0.1859 m on 46 changes (LOOK-014). So most of the disagreement the worked example reports is three flagged passes, and the recipe has no step that says to apply the product's quality gate before scoring.

data.about: pairing tolerance below the gauge's reporting interval
data.text: Seen while exploring. Pairing within 5 minutes keeps 31 of 52 passes, because the gauge reports every 15 minutes; 15 minutes keeps 50 and 60 minutes keeps all 52 with the same spread (0.298 m and 0.293 m) and, with the flag screen, a gain of 1.0121 and 1.0115. A tolerance tighter than the gauge interval only throws passes away.

data.takes: Read after the review pointed to it. Warns: provisional gauge values can be revised or withdrawn on approval, and statistics that mix provisional and approved values are unstable. All of 2024 here is provisional, and a later window would be too, so a test on it should record the approval status it ran on and not mix the two.

Read after the review pointed to it. About flow statistics at regulated gauges. Stage against a satellite height at the same place is not changed by regulation upstream; nothing taken beyond noting it was read.
